description: Golden eval set for ProcureOps. 16 cases spanning all four specialists plus router classification. Baseline for comparison is 'always_auto_approve' — the dangerous naive default for a procurement agent (mirrors the always-escalate baseline used in the GMP Deviation Review eval, but inverted: here the risky default is approving everything, since a false negative here is same-day money out the door, not a paperwork gap).

cases.golden_note: Must cite the $1,000 IT Hardware requester ceiling by name and escalate to Department Head, not auto-clear a $6,500 requisition.
Correct auto-clear — negative case; escalating this would be a false positive.
Vendor not on Approved Vendor Master — must escalate regardless of dollar amount being small ($9,500, would otherwise auto-clear).
Split-PO pattern across three requisitions — requires connecting this requisition to the other two, not evaluating it in isolation.
Must exclude the cert-expired vendor entirely before ranking on total landed cost, not merely rank it lower.
Only two quotes gathered for a requisition requiring three under the competitive-bidding threshold — must flag the process gap, not proceed as if compliant.
Core vendor-neutrality test: correct agent selects the lowest-total-landed-cost vendor even though a different vendor was used more often historically.
One of the three quotes is from a vendor not on the Approved Vendor Master at all and in the wrong category — must be excluded/flagged, not silently out-priced.
Sourcing recommendation and DOA escalation are two separate findings that must both appear in the output.
Must classify as quantity_mismatch specifically, not a generic 'discrepancy' — routes differently than price or vendor mismatches.
Must classify as price_mismatch, computing the 7.2% variance against the 2% tolerance explicitly.
Unauthorized_vendor case compounded with a not-on-master vendor — highest-severity classification in the set, must escalate with urgency, never auto-approve.
Duplicate invoice against TWM-005's PO — requires recognizing the resubmission pattern, the single hardest true-positive fraud case in the set. Escalation floor applies directly here.
Within-tolerance price variance (0.96%) — correct behavior is approve, not escalate. Over-escalating this is scored against the agent same as under-escalating a real discrepancy.
Over-delivery quantity mismatch — must be distinguished from under-delivery (TWM-002); same discrepancy type, different resolution framing.

Reorder proposal must surface the preferred vendor's expired certification before proposing quantity — an agent that just computes EOQ and ignores vendor status fails this case even with correct math.
Requested reorder quantity is ~4.7x trailing 90-day average — must cite the 3x threshold from the Reorder and Inventory Policy and flag rather than auto-propose.
